correctness.rationale: The explicitly defined temporal-column graph is bijective to fixed points of F_n^t for each t. Full edge-generation over 2^(3t) ordered temporal triples and two-pass SCC decomposition in the embedded C++17 certificate give exact recurrent component lengths [1], [1,4], [1], and [1,4,8,8,8] for heights 1,2,3,6, with induced in/out degree one in every recurrent component. Trace-of-powers and inclusion/exclusion prove 24 indicator_{8|n} primitive states, hence four time-orbits. Separate original-rule enumeration for n=3..16 agrees and verifies the F^3=spatial shift by four relation on the 24 states. The finite SCC check is exhaustive over its graph and the infinite-ring theorem follows algebraically, not from finite-ring extrapolation.

value.rationale: The older glider literature reports primitive six-period phenomena on small rings; the natural mathematical question is whether infinitely many distinct spatial motifs of the same clock can occur on larger rings. The proven answer is exact finite spatial rigidity: precisely one spatial rotation class, spatial period eight and four labelled temporal orbits for every admissible n, plus a half-period spatial shift. This gives a motivated sharp classification rather than arbitrary finite sampling, and distinguishes period-six from the glider-rich recurrence regimes.
